clue.text: Top military award worn in clubs, say

indicators.note: a medal worn in a suit of clothes is placed inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: clubs is an example of a suit of cards, hence SUIT
MM is the Military Medal, a British gallantry award

explanation.surface: A soldier's top decoration is pinned on while out at the clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs, say' suggests nightclubs, but it is one of the four card suits; 'worn in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point or peak of something is its summit.

indicators.note: the girl's name sits in the word for study, one piece within the other

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman is found poring over a book about artillery.
explanation.walkthrough: CON as 'study' is an old word much used in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon is a large gun, and ordnance is the collective word for artillery.

clue.text: Bulgarians end by arranging a charity event

indicators.note: arranging a set of letters puts them into a new order, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: People from Bulgaria finish off by organising a fundraiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder: BULGARIANS, END and BY are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale where people donate goods and buy others, the proceeds going to a good cause, is a classic British fundraiser.

parts.note: something popular is said to be 'in'
to nurse someone is to tend them, so nurses gives TENDS

explanation.surface: Fashionable carers of moderate wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' looks like a noun (money) after 'of', but it is the verb: to mean something is to plan it.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to have it as a purpose or plan.

clue.text: Double anxieties of accent and lineage?

parts.note: the accent on a syllable is its stress
a strain is a line of descent or breed

explanation.surface: A question about two worries: how one speaks and where one comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: The paired phrase names the pressure and tension of a demanding life, two worries coupled together.

clue.text: Doctor on violin, opens concerto, it's electrifying

parts.note: an Amati is a violin made by the famous Cremona family of luthiers

indicators.note: the letter that opens the word concerto is its first

explanation.surface: A medic playing the violin begins a concerto in a thrilling performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places DR above AMATI in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrilling, striking performance can be called electrifying or theatrical in its effect.

clue.text: County course has continuous heavy rain

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
to course is to flow or run, as liquid does, hence pour

explanation.surface: A golf course in an Irish county is under steady rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks like a noun (a golf course) but is the verb meaning to flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge, a torrential spell of rainfall.

indicators.note: to stew things is to mix them together, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A recipe in which nuts spoil a casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the anagram signal, but 'stew' is; NUTS, MAR and A are the letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is one of Indonesia's large islands, so a native of it is Indonesian.

definitions.meaning: to switch a machine on so it runs

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to switch on a device and to round angrily on someone.

clue.text: Run after soldiers or a sailor

indicators.note: the letter for run comes after the soldiers, so it follows them in the answer

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A dash behind the troops, or perhaps a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack tar is old slang for a seaman, so a tar is a sailor.

definitions.meaning: a mount is a hill or raised piece of ground
a cardinal is formally addressed as His or Your ...

explanation.definitionFit: The word means high ground and is also the formal title used for Catholic cardinals.

indicators.note: letters that are swimming are moving about, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stoat is seen paddling in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A mere is a lake, which suits the picture, but here IN and MERE are only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The stoat's white winter coat has its own name, and so the animal itself is called by it.

parts.note: reads like a night on the town, but means making things even or uniform

explanation.definitionFit: Making everything conform to one level or norm is evening it out.

parts.note: as means like, as in 'as good as gold'

indicators.note: originally points to the beginning of the word Simon, its first letter

explanation.surface: A foolish man, just like Simon in the nursery rhyme at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Simple Simon of the nursery rhyme suits 'silly fellow', but Simon gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or idiot is commonly called this donkey's name.

clue.text: Bad sort in instance of cataract

indicators.note: the bad sort is placed in the word for instance, within it

parts.note: an instance is a case, as in 'a case in point'
a cad is an ungentlemanly man, a bad sort

explanation.surface: A rogue as a medical example of eye trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cataract' suggests the eye condition, but here it is a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataract is a large waterfall, and a waterfall falling in stages is another name for it.

clue.text: Weird bachelor retires in the ordinary way

indicators.note: to retire is to draw back, so the abbreviation for bachelor is turned round

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
normal as a noun is the usual state of things, as in 'back to normal'

explanation.surface: A strange single man goes to bed at the usual time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retires' turns the degree letters round, giving AB; 'bachelor' tempts as the definition of a single man, but 'Weird' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something strange or odd departs from what is usual, so it is not normal.

definitions.meaning: the pieces in the board game of draughts (checkers)

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for opposing and also the round playing pieces in draughts, known as checkers in America.

clue.text: Foreign coin in burial vase of fabulous creature

indicators.note: the rearranged coin goes in the burial vase, one inside the other

parts.note: an urn holds a person's ashes

indicators.note: foreign suggests strange or unfamiliar, so the letters of coin are altered

explanation.surface: An exotic coin found in a funeral urn depicting a mythical beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' turns COIN into NICO, which goes into URN.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-horned horse of legend is a fabulous, that is mythical, beast.

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is drawn out of the letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Verse delivered by the Greek poet Sappho.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappho was a Greek lyric poet, which makes 'lines' look literal; the answer straddles her name and the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric poem is a set of lines of verse.

parts.note: a saloon is a type of car, called a sedan in America
teacher's pets are favourites

explanation.surface: A telling-off for the regulars of a saloon bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saloon' suggests a bar, but it is a car body type.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone onto the carpet is to reprimand them, so the verb means to scold.

clue.text: Opening lines making epicureans laugh wildly?

indicators.note: wildly means the letters go everywhere, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Words at the start that make gourmets roar with laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: The first address given by a new president or office-holder is the start of their term in words.

parts.note: a gumshoe is a detective, a private eye
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A detective has been permitted to use a spyhole.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round hole, such as one for a lace, is something one might peep through.

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: Gossiping in a church at a north-east English port.
explanation.walkthrough: Tynemouth is a town at the mouth of the River Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fond of chat is talkative.

clue.text: Soldiers surrounding deserter without a charge

indicators.note: the soldiers surround the deserter, putting it inside

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is one who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Troops capture a runaway but bring no charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a charge' suggests a legal charge, but it means free of payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for free of cost, used of things given at no price.

parts.note: par is the standard level, as in 'up to par'

indicators.note: to churn is to stir violently, so the letters of means are mixed up

explanation.surface: The usual way to make cheese, by churning milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to churn' rearranges MEANS into MESAN; 'Standard' looks like a cheese grade but gives the golfing term for the usual score.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard Italian cheese from the Parma region.

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another comes after it

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A single remark made on a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: In cards and dice, the single pip is the one.

indicators.note: strange means odd or abnormal, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: The odd charm of a coastal inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' suggests a stretch of coast, but it is the bay tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay tree, whose leaves were woven into victors' wreaths, is the same plant.

indicators.note: the word for free is placed in the shelters, within them

parts.note: tents are temporary shelters
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: Weapons released in an encampment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missiles' names the Trident weapon system; 'free' is the verb RID, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Trident is the name of the submarine-launched nuclear missile system used by Britain and the US.
